Accessing Theme Management

You Access this page through the App Management Tabs. From here you can manage what the current app’s theme, this includes the logos that are displayed in the site’s header and the colours that are used throughout the application.

 

The UI

When you go to the “Theming” tab you’re greeted with something that looks like this:

Here, the “Brand Logo” is the logo that is displayed at the top left of the screen and the “Project Logo” is typically the logo of the project, for example, for this demo app this could incorporate the words “Corporate LinX Demo”. We also support having a background animation which is mostly visible on the Login and Home pages of the site which can be uploaded by dragging and dropping your image from your local file explorer to the upload box. You may also change the existing files in DMS by dragging and dropping a new image over the previews. From this tab, you can also manage the themes that exist in the current application.

 

Creating a Theme

This grid is where you manage the themes that exist in the application, to create a new theme you click on the “New” button which will bring up a dialog that looks something like this:

Creating a new theme is simple as it only requires you to give it a name and click the “Confirm” button. Creating a “Test” theme you can see that it’s added into the grid:

 

Updating a Theme

To update the theme that was just created, you click on the “Edit” button on the relevant row, this will bring up a dialog that looks something like this:

 

Colours

To understand what each of these colours represent, the dialog is broken down into two sections, “Base Colours” and “Chart Colours”

The “Base Colours” section is where you set the “main” colours that are used across the application, most obviously, the “Primary” colour defines the colour of the header bar that goes across the screen and the “Secondary” colour defines the colour of any headings for charts or dialogs for example. The “Background” colour determines the colour of the background of the site as a whole. We allow for two different text colours so that they can be used in situations where the contrast maybe too low for the users reading it. The “Links” colour determines what colour any links within the portal will be displayed as and the “Margins” sets up the value for the default margins across the portal, which determines how much spaces there is between the components.

The “Chart Colours” section is where you set up the colours for the charts across the application, ideally these should all be different colours and not similar shades of the same colour as this will mean that the data displayed in chart format is more difficult to read.

To change any of the colours in this section of the dialog, you click onto the dropdown that corresponds to the colour you want to edit, this will bring up a dialog that looks something like this:

The rectangles in the top right are there for previewing the colour you currently have selected. You can change the colour by either using the colour picker using your cursor, or by entering a HEX colour code which is often provided to you on a style sheet.

Font

Clicking on the “Font” tab within this dialog displays something that looks like this:

The “Size” can be selected using the slider, as you can see in screenshot the size is set to 11 px and the “Family” determines what font that’s used across the portal.

Border

Clicking on the “Border” tab within this dialog displays something that looks like this:

The “Style” dropdown allows a default border style to be set across the portal, these borders will be displayed around every component that you see. It would be recommended to keep this value low at potentially 1 or 2px which you can set with the “Width” slider below. The “Colour” of these borders are determined by the colour picker in this dialog. The “Radius” sets the CSS property, border-radius. this is what determines how rounded the corners of the border are displayed, small values result in more pointed-looking corners and higher values will make them much more rounded.

Notifications

Clicking on the “Notifications” tab within this dialog displays something that looks like this:

This section of the dialog defines what colours the notifications appear are. These can be fully customised using the colour pickers within this section, it’s important to ensure that the text colour isn’t too dark or too light in comparison to the background colour as this would mean that the text is less readable and users may have issues reading the description of the error they’ve received.

Shadows

Clicking on the “Shadows” tab within this dialog displays something that looks like this:

The “Horizontal Offset” slider determines how far in pixels the shadow appears to the left or the right, the “Vertical Offset” defines how far in pixels the shadow appears to the top or the bottom of the container. “Blur Radius” determines how blurry the shadow appears, setting this to 0 will mean that the shadow will look like a solid black border. The higher this value is set to the further the colour is diffused across. The “Colour” of this shadow can be set to whatever you want, however if you want it to look like a more “natural” shadow then this should be set to black or a dark grey colour.

Etc

Clicking on the “Etc” tab within this dialog displays something that looks like this:

The “Paint Login Mid” sets the login component on the login page of the portal to be displayed in the middle of the screen and “Paint Login Bottom" sets it such that the login component is displayed at the bottom of the page. It is supported such that we can use a flag or an image display to display what cultures can be selected within the portal, this can be changed by selecting “Picture” in the “Culture Flag Layout” dropdown.

To save any changes made within this dialog, you just click the “Save” button. This will save any changes to the application’s configuration and they should be now visible in the portal.

 

Deleting a Theme

You can delete a theme in the themes grid by clicking the “Delete” button on the row of the theme you want to delete.

This will delete the theme from the application’s config and remove it from the grid.
